sendTest: Monday.com just cut 620 jobs and its own founders say AI was not the reason.
centralClaim: Monday.com is cutting about 620 jobs, roughly 20% of its workforce, in a restructuring its SEC filing ties to an AI-driven growth strategy, while co-founder Eran Zinman told employees the cuts were not made to replace people with AI.

corroboration.quote: On Wednesday, the company said in an SEC filing that it will lay off about 20% of its workforce, or just over 600 employees, as part of a "restructuring plan" tied to its "ongoing transformation of its product, marketing, and go-to-market strategy" in support of "a leaner, more focused operating model" as it continues investing in its "AI-driven growth strategy."
Monday.com is cutting roughly 20 percent of its global workforce, about 620 people, as the Israeli project management company restructures around what it calls its AI Work Platform.

caption:
620 people lost their jobs at Monday.com, and the company's own founders say AI was not the reason.

The filing and the letter went out in the same week. To the regulator, the cut was a leaner operating model in support of an AI-driven growth strategy. To the staff, it was not made to reduce costs or replace people with AI. Both sentences describe the same 620 jobs.

Monday.com is not an outlier, and that is the part worth reading twice. The Financial Times counted nearly 140,000 US tech jobs cut since the start of this year. It also found that the companies naming AI as a factor went on to underperform the Nasdaq by almost 10% in the 30 trading days after they said so.

The caveat, plainly: nobody outside the company can say which of those 620 jobs would still exist without an AI strategy, and the filing does not break it down. Underperforming a stock index is not proof that a company was lying either.

Has your employer used the word AI while cutting people, and did anybody in the room believe it?
